P1.evidence: Notes acknowledged but not reflected back — 'I have a couple notes on you here. Nothing crazy' — so P1a is the weak variant again. Four-part frame delivered: 'get a super solid sense of where you're at in your fitness journey, what you're looking to accomplish, what's kind of missing between the two... And then from there, we can have a chat about what a potential coaching program could look like for you.' Frame agreement asked and given: 'Sound good?' / 'Yeah, cool. Sounds great.' Open question run: 'What do you feel we could potentially help you with? Give me the overview here.'

P2.evidence: Age, height and weight collected directly at 00:10:38. Body composition satisfaction scored one to ten and time-bounded — 'how happy are you with like your body composition right now? One to 10' / 'a four, five' / 'When did you start really noticing that?' — which is a strong P2f. Nutrition asked and covered in full at 00:20:05. The weaknesses: work was established but the desk-versus-feet distinction was volunteered rather than asked, and the rep only asked what he consults on at 01:03:20, nearly an hour in. Health and injuries were both handled by a single generic catch-all at the end of discovery — 'is there anything else at all you feel I might need to know... anything health, fitness related' — which happened to produce a clean answer but is a weaker variant of two separate scripted checks, and hereditary conditions were never asked about. Training week was discussed as intention ('my goal is to basically run three to four times a week and train three to four times a week') but the actual current week was never pinned down, despite the prospect having been ill and out for two months. Sleep and energy were never asked about at all.

P3.evidence: The surface layer is the best in this batch. 'what's the ultimate goal with your fitness right now, man?' produced strength and mobility; the one-to-ten body composition question gave a concrete gap; the strength-mobility-or-something-else menu was effectively run. The bridge was asked well and twice: 'what's the drive behind really taking fitness seriously, right now?' and 'what actually shifted where it's like, hey, dude, it's actually time to get this handled?' The deep layer is where it stops. The prospect handed over the entire deep motivation unprompted — 'we're talking about having kids... I want to stay capable and healthy for my wife and potential kids... then that will be a habit that will carry on' — and the rep's complete response was 'Yeah. I love it, man. Yeah.' He never asked who else this impacts, never developed the wife, never developed the children they are planning, and never returned to any of it later when he needed leverage. Reflect-back was done well twice, including 'it seems like a lot of areas of your life are dialed in. Fitness is really like a holistic thing for you', which the prospect accepted with 'That makes a lot more sense.'

P4.evidence: Past attempts arrived largely unprompted — small group training, HIIT, Byron Bay kettlebell work, ultramarathon phases — though 'How's your attitude been around your body the last six months to a year? What's that been like?' did properly surface what happened with them. The needs question ran cleanly: 'what are we potentially looking for when it comes to coaching? Like, what are we needing? What's missing?' and the prospect named the gap precisely — 'I don't have the technical understanding nor the time to create a program, and I need feedback, I guess. That's a big thing.' P4f is the notable miss and it mattered later: this prospect describes himself as self-motivated and happy to run his own programme, which makes 'The information isn't the problem. Why can't you stick to it on your own?' the single most load-bearing question available, and it was never asked.

P5.evidence: There is no consequence frame on this call. The two-year question was never asked, the settle-for test was never run, and the why-not follow-up never happened. The only P5 move present is the line in the sand, delivered as a soft reflection rather than a question — 'Sounds like it's a bit of a time to draw a line in the sand. Is that kind of what I'm hearing with all this?' — which drew a mild 'Pretty much. Yeah.' The rep went from goals straight into the offer, so when value resistance arrived forty minutes later there was no cost of inaction to return to, and P6c had nowhere to send him back to.

P6.evidence: Both scripted questions ran and both were well phrased. P6b came before the price, correctly: 'provided we can sort out the logistics... are we actually willing to go all in, commit 100%, like do all the workouts, follow the routine?' P6a ran after price as an isolation: 'finances aside, man... do you actually feel like everything that we've gone to in the program that we've laid out can actually not only create this massive transformation physically for you, but actually teach you how to take your, like, through the turmoil and the inconsistency?' followed by 'Why do you feel like it can help you?' P6c fails. The answer to P6b was explicitly conditional — 'at this point, it's absolutely. And of course, depending on the program and what it looks like' — and the rep moved to price on it anyway. Once hesitation surfaced he never returned to Phase 5, which is what the check requires, though in fairness there was no Phase 5 to return to.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and declined, so the payment and onboarding sequence was never reachable. The rep did correctly pre-frame the mechanics before quoting — 'we just, you know, we process it, usually just grab a credit card number from you, punch it into our process... We book you in with Trevor for your onboarding call, you fill out an onboarding form between now and then' — but no step was executed because there was no sale.

objection_plays.detail: Money was raised in substance at 00:55:14 via the currency conversion. The isolate move ran, and ran twice and well: 'finances aside, man' at 00:50:17 and 'let's just say finances was out of the picture entirely... would you actually jump on the program?' at 01:13:20, which produced a clean 'Yeah, yeah, totally, yeah, without a question.' Everything after the isolate was skipped. No open-and-honest-conversation permission question, no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. Most consequentially the payment-plan move — 'Most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up. Want to explore making it work?' — never ran, even though the prospect's objection was specifically about a single upfront outlay and he twice named month-to-month or week-to-week as what he expected. Instead of the scripted plan the rep improvised an unnamed cheaper tier and offered to email options.

Think-about-it was raised at least four times, first at 00:56:31 and most plainly at 01:11:15. Two scripted moves ran: 'do you feel this CAN get you to your goal' as part of the isolation, and 'what makes you feel it can' via 'Why do you feel like it can help you?' The nothing-else-keeping-you move also ran at 01:00:11: 'is there anything else at all that's keeping you from being less than 100% certain that like, this is the right thing and now is the right time?' The core of the play never ran — no 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here', no future-self question. The rep instead expressed his own confusion twice, which cost him the frame.

The real objection has no scripted play: the package is the wrong shape. Not price, not timing, not doubt about efficacy. 'I understand the need to wrap it in a bundle, but it just might not suit me' and 'If it's projected and it's like... a class in level one kettlebells, or level two kettlebells, and you have one-on-one coaching, here's your program... then I'd walk in and be like, okay, cool, this is the expectation of what is required.' He rated the presented programme six out of ten and then described the ten out of ten in detail: three staged programmes across six months with the education layer on the back end rather than front-loaded. Proposed label: offer_shape_mismatch. This belongs alongside the clinical-fit and cheaper-alternative gaps already documented in the playbook — the script assumes the blocker is capacity or conviction, and has nothing for a prospect who wants the same thing packaged differently. The rep's improvisation ran toward an unpriced discount rather than toward the staged structure the prospect had just specified.

notes: Presentation and pillar delivery were the strongest in this batch, and the price was quoted correctly. Two structural failures cost the call. First, no consequence frame at all — P5 is essentially absent, so there was no cost of inaction to anchor value against and nowhere to return when resistance came. Second, the rep mis-diagnosed the objection: the prospect said four times that money was not the constraint and that he pays for expertise on principle, and the rep concluded 'it really just does come down to the finances, basically' anyway, then never ran the payment plan the playbook provides. Coach specifically on developing the deep why — this prospect volunteered his wife, planned children and legacy at 00:24:04 and it was answered with 'I love it, man' and never used again.
